Net income was 3,100 in FY2023, 3,600 in FY2024 and 3,900 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2023-FY2025]. CONFLICT: the analyst's summary of the borrower's FY2025 letter states "Net income rose to $4.2 million" [D1, §6], while the spread shows FY2025 net income of 3,900 [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2025]. Customer A accounted for 28% of FY2024 revenue and 31% of FY2025 revenue, and the top five customers accounted for 64% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5].

### 3.2 Leverage and Debt Service [M]

Total funded debt was 22,400 at FY2023, 20,900 at FY2024 and 19,800 at FY2025 [D1, Table 2: Total funded debt, FY2023-FY2025]. Total leverage was 2.60x in FY2023, 2.20x in FY2024 and 1.90x in FY2025 [D1, Table 2: Total leverage, FY2023-FY2025]. For reference, FY2022 total funded debt was 22,500 and total leverage was 2.85x [D3, Part B §3].

FY2025 total funded debt of 19,800 consisted of the Meridian term loan 5,600, the Meridian revolver 3,200 and the equipment notes (Prairie Equipment Finance) 11,000 [D1, Table 4: all rows, FY2025].

Debt service (P+I) was 4,500 in FY2023, 4,550 in FY2024 and 4,800 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Debt service (P+I), FY2023-FY2025]. Unfunded capex was 1,200 in FY2023, 1,300 in FY2024 and 1,400 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Unfunded capex, FY2023-FY2025]. Cash taxes were 1,000 in FY2023, 1,150 in FY2024 and 1,250 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Cash taxes, FY2023-FY2025]. DSCR was 1.42x in FY2023, 1.55x in FY2024 and 1.61x in FY2025 [D1, Table 2: DSCR, FY2023-FY2025]. FY2022 DSCR was 1.31x [D3, Part B §3].

Definitions as spread: total leverage is total funded debt divided by EBITDA, and DSCR is (EBITDA minus unfunded capex minus cash taxes) divided by debt service (P+I) [D1, §2, Definitions as spread]. The draft agreement defines "EBITDA" as net income plus interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and non-cash charges, and defines "Total Funded Debt" as indebtedness for borrowed money, capital lease obligations and the Equipment Notes [D2, §1.1]. The spread export does not state whether its EBITDA figure includes non-cash charges or whether its total funded debt includes capital lease obligations [D1, §2, Definitions as spread].

Per the FY2025 compliance certificate dated April 28, 2026, under the existing 2023 credit agreement, total leverage was 1.90x against a maximum of 3.50x and DSCR was 1.61x against a minimum of 1.20x, and the borrower was in compliance with both financial covenants [D1, §7].

Liquidity (cash plus availability) was 3,900 at FY2023 and 4,900 at FY2024 [D1, Table 2: Liquidity (cash + availability), FY2023-FY2024].

Not in provided documents: FY2025 year-end cash balance and FY2025 liquidity. The spread export states the FY2025 year-end cash balance was not included and that the borrower will provide year-end bank statements with the Q3 2026 package [D1, Table 2, Footnote *]. These figures would normally appear in the CreditLens spread export or the borrower's year-end bank statements.

Average operating deposits with Meridian were $4.1 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026 [D5, ¶2].

### 3.4 Pro Forma for Proposed Facility [M]

The proposed facility is $18.0M in total: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver [D1, Table 3 note]. Term loan proceeds refinance the existing Meridian term loan 5,600, fund the plant expansion 6,000 and pay fees 400, for a total of 12,000 [D1, Table 3 note].

On an FY2025 basis, pro forma total funded debt is 26,200, made up of the proposed term loan 12,000, the Meridian revolver 3,200 and the equipment notes 11,000 [D1, Table 3: Total funded debt; Table 3 note]. Pro forma total leverage is 2.52x [D1, Table 3: Total leverage]. Pro forma debt service is 5,600 [D1, Table 3: Debt service]. Pro forma DSCR is 1.38x [D1, Table 3: DSCR].

The Term Loan matures five years after the Closing Date and amortizes on a seven-year schedule, with the unpaid principal balance due at maturity [D2, §2.1(a)]. The Revolving Commitment terminates, and all revolving loans are due, five years after the Closing Date [D2, §2.1(b)].
